text:
rita: Starting canary for tango9b-int4 on Dedicated. Saw 2 OOMs on long exports (~800-1100 tokens). Logs show big KV jumps. Anyone quick mitigation?

omar: Paste the log + config? my money is on variable-length batching creating fragmentation.

rita: Snippet + cfg: 
```
[2026-08-11T09:10:02Z] req=77a model=tango9b-int4 max_new_tokens=1024 batch=3 mem_delta=+3.5GB slab_frag=0.48
[2026-08-11T09:10:02Z] gpu0: OOM at kv_alloc serving/allocator/slab.cc:308
```
serving.yml: `max_batch_size: 3, max_new_tokens_default: 1024, kv_eviction: lazy, slot_compaction: disabled`

dina: Short ops playbook I've used: (1) drop batch size to 1-2; (2) enable length bucketing to keep similar max_new_tokens together; (3) enable slot compaction and switch eviction to eager; (4) set slab_soft_reserve ~400MB.

omar: Agreed. I rolled a tiny canary tweak at 09:18: `max_batch_size=2, length_bucketing=true, max_new_tokens_default=320, kv_eviction=eager, slot_compaction=enabled, slab_soft_reserve=400MB`.

perf-bot: Canary snapshot @09:40: p99 down from 1.9s->1.05s, OOMs=0/30m, slab_frag=0.31, headroom +1.2GB.

dina: Also note quant-quality: int4 tends to drift on very long outputs. Limiting default max_new_tokens improves stability and often reduces the int4->fp16 rouge gap. Schedule a quick quant sweep (int4 vs int8-hybrid) for long-form.

rita: Created ticket ML-13033 for defaults + rollout and ML-13034 for the sweep. On-call SOP: if OOMs recur -> set max_batch_size=1, max_new_tokens_default=128, enable compaction immediately and escalate.

(End)
